thread:
maria: Heads up — a customer hit a burst this morning and got a flurry of 504s + occasional 502s. They reported timeouts around 120s, lots of upstream gateway 5xx. Looks like scale-up lag.

sam: Which tenant? any repro steps from the customer?

maria: tenant=acme-inc, spike at 08:12 UTC. Customer says ~300 concurrent requests suddenly. They sent one sample request for a streaming chat call.

alex: I pulled the platform metrics — queue depth jumped, KEDA ScaledObject metrics flapped. HPA stayed at 2, KEDA tried to scale but pod_count stayed low because readiness probe failing during model init (pods stuck NotReady for ~90s).

jess: Oncall digging into events now. Initial suspicion: readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds is too short for large models, so KEDA/HPA think pods are up but they don't accept traffic until model load completes.

ops-bot: deploy event: new revision started at 2024-11-02T08:05:12Z. Scaling annotation on workload: "keda.sh/trigger-auth: enabled".

maria: Customer logs show a sequence: gateway returns 504 after queuing ~30s, then client retries and sees 502 from auth service, then 504 again. Billing auth spikes coincided with token rotation 08:10 (we had a brief cached creds miss).

sam: Can you paste the relevant events and the scaledobject? minimal commands to reproduce locally?

maria: Repro (on staging):
1) start a small load generator to simulate a sudden burst: `hey -n 600 -c 300 http://staging-host/api/v1/generate`
2) watch scaledobject: `kubectl -n prod get scaledobject acme-gateway -o yaml`
3) check pod events: `kubectl describe deploy acme-gateway`

maria: Events snippet:
```
Warning  Unhealthy  90s   kubelet, ip-10-0-1-3  Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
Normal   Created    64s   kubelet, ip-10-0-1-3  Created container model-server
Normal   Pulling    63s   kubelet, ip-10-0-1-3  Pulling image
Warning  BackOff    12s   kubelet, ip-10-0-1-3  Back-off restarting failed container
```

alex: Readiness returned 503 during model initialization. The runtime returns 503 until KV cache and model weights loaded. HPA sees pod ready=false so KEDA keeps querying external metrics; if KEDA polling interval + cooldown + minReplicaCount are small, you can get delayed effective scale.

jess: I see in the deployment annotations: `redwood.com/prewarm: "false"` and `autoscaling.minReplicas: "1"` for this tenant. For bursty tenants we usually set minReplicas=3 or enable prewarm. Also KEDA trigger polling was default 30s — combined adds up.

sam: Two likely contributors: (1) minReplicaCount too low for burst; (2) readiness probe incorrectly signals 503 instead of delaying AcceptTraffic. Quick mitigation: bump minReplicas to 3 for acme, increase readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to 120, and enable prewarm image if available.

maria: Agreed. Also customer saw auth 502s — looks like our auth backend hit request queue limits while scaling. Recommend increasing auth token service concurrency and add graceful fallback for short auth failures (retry with jitter).

ops-bot: patch applied by jess at 2024-11-02T08:20:03Z: `kubectl -n prod patch deploy acme-gateway --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood.com/prewarm":"true"}}}}}'`

maria: After patch, observed new pods starting with preloaded model image. Time to Ready dropped from ~90s to ~22s. Gateway 504s subsided within 3 minutes. Customer confirms lower error rate.

alex: Follow-up actionable items: [ ] add guardrail in template to set minReplicas>=2 for tenants with burst_profile=high, [ ] change readiness probe to return 429 (or hold connection) until model is ready to accept traffic, [ ] reduce KEDA polling to 10s for ScaledObjects with critical latency SLOs, [ ] add auth service token cache warming during prewarm.

jess: I'll create a quick runbook and a customer-facing note summarizing root cause (scale-up lag + readiness probe mismatch + transient auth token miss) and the mitigation we applied.

maria: Customer success wants a short timeline and repro for their ticket. Jess, can you paste the runbook link when ready?

jess: Posted runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/incident-4412345678 (internal). Short summary to CS: patched prewarm + bumped min replicas → decreased cold init 90s→22s → reduced gateway 5xx.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-9823 updated: status -> escalated -> resolved-pending-customer-verification.

sam: Nice work team. Can we add a periodic test to simulate sudden bursts on canary tenants to catch this pre-deploy? :eyes:

maria: +1 :thumbsup:

alex: I'll open a follow PR for autoscale template guardrails and KEDA tuning.

jess: Closing thread once CS confirms customer ok.
